analysis.primary_contrast: developmental - best_non_developmental, where best_non_developmental is the available model (excluding random and developmental) with the lowest TRAIN objective; paired over held-out MCPL participants.
analysis.primary_metric_definition: Mean over held-out MCPL participants of each participant's mean negative log-likelihood (natural log) of their actual choices under teacher forcing, after lapse mixing. Lower is better. Chance = ln 9 = 2.1972 (MCPL), ln 4 = 1.3863 (IGT).
secondary_contrasts: best_adaptive - best_static (each chosen on TRAIN), MCPL
robustness: primary and secondary contrasts repeated on split seeds 1 and 2
analysis.status_rule: passed if ci_high < 0 and estimate <= -0.02; failed if ci_low > -0.02; inconclusive otherwise, or if the developmental class is not available in the build.

falsification_criterion: The hypothesis fails if the paired 95% bootstrap CI over held-out participants for (developmental NLL - best non-developmental NLL) excludes improvements of at least 0.02 nats per choice (ci_low > -0.02), or if the developmental learner is worse (ci_low > 0).
hypothesis: A developmental learner (Tier-2 policy, hpe.development) predicts held-out human choices in multiple-cue probability learning better than the strongest non-developmental model, including static models fitted to other participants and the memory-only / plain-RL baselines.
title: Do our policy classes predict held-out human learning choices (Psych-101 MCPL and IGT)?
validity_notes: Teacher-forced one-step-ahead likelihood measures predictive fit to human choice sequences, not generative realism.
Registry classes are not tuned beyond lapse/reward scale; reference cognitive models get small grids. This favours the reference models.
Participants are adults in short laboratory tasks; this says nothing about life-course development or the simulator's world.
Psych-101 transcripts were used to train the Centaur language model; irrelevant here because no language model is used, noted for context.
MCPL cue encoding (one-hot + scalar, 12 features) is a modelling choice shared by all models.
